facts.fact: 说笑话本身是一门独立技艺，不只是把笑话语念出来
facts.anchor: There’s more to making people laugh than just reading a joke out loud.

facts.fact: 最败兴的是把笑话拖很久却把包袱砸掉，前面全白讲
facts.anchor: Nothing is more frustrating than listening to someone stretch out a joke for ages and then absolutely botch the landing.

facts.fact: 包袱一旦讲坏，听众花掉的时间就被白白浪费，作者称之为偷窃
facts.anchor: A mangled punchline turns a lot of what you just listened to into wasted time. That’s basically theft.

facts.fact: 荒谬设定必须先被当真：熊不会走进酒吧，但讲与听的人都要暂时搁置怀疑
facts.anchor: Bears don’t walk into bars, but everyone involved in the joke-telling process needs to suspend their disbelief briefly, just enough to go with it.

facts.fact: 讲笑话的人知道走向，容易误以为听众也知道，于是赶得过快，听众跟不上
facts.anchor: If you know where a joke is going, it’s easy to feel like everyone does, but if you rattle through it like you’ve got a gun to your head, people are going to struggle to follow what’s going on.

facts.fact: 要留停顿让信息被消化，讲的是故事而不是念条款
facts.anchor: Take your time. Leave pauses for information to be digested. You’re telling a story, not running through a set of terms and conditions.

facts.fact: 铺垫越长，兑现越爽；而笑话独有之处是铺垫越长，完全不给兑现也越爽（为无包袱笑话埋线）
facts.anchor: The bigger the buildup, the more satisfying the payoff. But also, uniquely to jokes, the bigger the buildup, the more satisfying the absolute and total lack of a payoff.

facts.fact: 用《大白鲨》和整本高亮笔作比：脏话这类强效果必须省着用
facts.anchor: You barely see the shark through most of Jaws. You can’t write a book completely in highlighter.

facts.fact: 有时讲砸本身就是最好笑：小孩自己笑到讲不完第一句，技艺上很糟，却极其动人
facts.anchor: A kid laughing their head off, unable to get through the first line of a completely rubbish gag because they know what’s coming, is clearly a terrible bit of joke-telling, but it’s absolutely joyous.
